Have you heard of the “Ship of Theseus”? When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. In this situation, could we still call it the Ship of Theseus? Well, we are living examples of the Ship of Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing to become new versions of ourselves. This means that our future selves may be very different from who we are now. Then how can we create a future we’ll be proud of? I have some advice for you. First, actively envision the kind of person you want to become in the future. To do this, spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious. Second, when expressing your views online or with friends, remember that your future self might disagree with your current opinions. So, be respectful of other people’s opinions and don’t just assume that you are always right. Finally, your future self will have strengths and wisdom that you may lack today. Even if you can’t do something now, you might be able to in the future. So, don’t be afraid of new challenges. Be brave! The skiers jump from the height of 90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the air for about five to seven seconds. While they are in the air, they are influenced by “lift,” an upward force produced by air on a fast-moving object. When the force of lift is balanced with the force of gravity, the skiers can fly for long distances. The key factors for them to increase lift and jumping distance are increasing their speed, spreading out their bodies and skis, and adjusting their body angle. As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance as well as their style, skiers have tried many techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming to achieve longer distances. In the beginning, most skiers simply stood upright throughout their jump. Later, this upright style was replaced by the Kongsberger style. The skiers’ upper body was bent at the hips, with their arms extended in front of them and their skis parallel to each other. This technique doubled the average jumping distance. Everything changed in 1985, however, when Swedish jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style. In this style, the skiers position their skis into a “V” shape with their heads placed between the skis. This modification increases the surface area and creates more lift, leading to even greater jumping distances. Wind tunnel tests showed that the V style (A)____________ air lift by 28%, which means that skiers can stay in the air longer. This style also enables skiers to land at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury. The V style was not immediately adopted by the skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed and received fewer style points for breaking the standard of parallel skis. However, the technique proved so (B)____________ that by 1992 all Olympic medalists were using it.
answer: standards

To make social media a positive part of your daily life, it is important to use it mindfully with some guidelines. First, don’t let social media consume all your time and attention. A quick and easy way to do this is to set limits on your usage or take regular breaks from social media. This will free up your time and energy to engage in activities outside the online world. Second, keep in mind that social media is a tool to network with others, not a platform for competition. When you start to feel unpopular or inferior, remember that what you see online presents only the highlights of other people’s lives and does not reflect their entire story. If you still feel envious, use that emotion as motivation that helps you with your personal growth. By following these rules, you can make the most of social media and feel more at ease in your digital interactions. answer: (A) limits (B) network

The Flip Turn in Swimming Up until the 1936 Olympics, swimmers used an open turn. They touched the wall with one or two hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from the wall by bending their legs. However, open turns had the critical disadvantage of disrupting the swimmers’ flow and speed. This problem was resolved by an American high school student named Al Vande Weghe. While practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which caused him to slow down. To overcome this drawback, he devised a technique that is now known as a flip turn. He would make a forward roll first to change direction and then kick against the wall to speed ahead. This technique allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and momentum as possible. His willingness to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off. Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in freestyle and backstroke races. (1) What was the critical disadvantage of open turns? → The critical disadvantage of open turns was ____________________________________________________. (2) What did the technique known as the flip turn allow Al Vande Weghe to do? → It ____________________________________________________ ______________________________________________________.
answer: disrupting the swimmers’ flow and speed allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and momentum as possible
